name: Stabroek, Georgetown
name_zh: 乔治敦 · 斯塔布鲁克
note: 1812 年 4 月，英国怪才博物学家查尔斯·沃特顿从当时还叫“斯塔布鲁克”的这座荷兰人建的小城出发，深入德梅拉拉和埃塞奎博的雨林，一去就是四趟旅行，写成了《南美漫游记》。他赤脚走路、睡吊床、拿自己试箭毒，还骑过鳄鱼。斯塔布鲁克后来并入英属圭亚那的首府乔治敦，名字留在了河边那座铸铁钟楼大市场上
note_en: In April 1812 the eccentric English naturalist Charles Waterton set out from this little Dutch-built town, then called Stabroek, into the rainforests of Demerara and Essequibo. He made four journeys in all and wrote them up as Wanderings in South America: he went barefoot, slept in a hammock, tested arrow poison, and once rode a cayman. Stabroek was later absorbed into Georgetown, the capital of British Guiana, and its name lives on in the great cast-iron market with the clock tower by the river

name: Bartica, Essequibo River
name_zh: 埃塞奎博河 · 巴蒂卡
note: 巴蒂卡在埃塞奎博河与马扎鲁尼河交汇处，是进入圭亚那内陆的门户。沃特顿第三次旅行就沿埃塞奎博河上行去找大凯门鳄，在第一道瀑布上游的沙洲上，他纵身跳上被钓上岸的鳄鱼背，把它的两条前腿扭到背上当缰绳——这段“骑鳄”成了他一生最有名的故事。他还在这条河上救过一只困在沙滩上的二趾树懒，送它爬回树上。今天从巴蒂卡坐船上溯，仍是去内陆瀑布和雨林的主要路线
note_en: Bartica, where the Essequibo meets the Mazaruni, is the gateway to the interior of Guyana. On his third journey Waterton went up the Essequibo looking for a big cayman, and on a sandbank above the first falls he leapt onto the back of one his men had hauled ashore, twisting its forelegs up behind it for a bridle. The cayman ride became the most famous story of his life. On the same river he rescued a two-toed sloth stranded on the sand and helped it back up into the trees. Boats from Bartica are still the main way up the river into the falls and forests of the interior
